comparator.name: Science and Innovation Management
comparator.route: Energy & Transport with Innovation in Firms and Markets
comparator.sourceNotes: Utrecht requires 75 EC of common courses, 30 EC in one science domain, a 15 EC thesis in that domain, 15 EC in one innovation learning line and 45 EC of profiling electives. The example uses Energy & Transport and Innovation in Firms and Markets.
components: Research Methods for Science and Innovation
Introduction to Energy and Material Analysis
Management of Energy and Transport Innovations
Innovation Strategies of Firms and Entrepreneurs
Include at least 7.5 EC at advanced level to reach the degree’s 45 EC advanced-level requirement in this example.

routeSelection.route: Energy & Transport with Innovation in Firms and Markets
routeSelection.basis: The regulations require a complete domain and a complete learning line. The first-listed domain and learning line form the example, selected independently of the UCR plans.

core: Combining natural science with innovation management across science, business and government
Turning scientific discoveries into useful innovations and understanding why technologies succeed or fail
Entrepreneurship, firm strategy and the financing of innovative technologies
Project-based innovation work with societal partners
Research design, statistics and evaluation methods for innovation studies
Economics, organisation theory and management of innovation
Public policy, regulation, societal transitions and social consequences of technological change
Mathematics, systems analysis and digital/data foundations for innovation analysis
Financing and commercial assessment of emerging technologies
Ethical and societal assessment of new technologies
adjacent: Energy and transport innovation, energy technologies, materials and conversions, renewable systems and clean mobility
Life-science and medical innovation, molecular and human biology, medicines and new medical technologies
questions: Illustrative current innovation cases used by the programme (care robots, patenting a medicine, neighbourhood batteries, offshore wind, heat pumps and DNA modification)
Possible graduate directions in innovation research, consultancy, policy, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, sustainability and emerging-technology management

Examines institutions, collective action and governance of sustainability transitions.
Uses life-cycle assessment and circular economy to evaluate products and processes.

Develops remote sensing, spatial data and environmental observation for evidence gathering.

alternatives.label: Science, Technology and Innovation Management
alternatives.labelReason: Study how scientific discoveries become useful innovations. Combine entrepreneurship, economics and digital strategy with research methods, then use climate, resource use and biomedicine to explore different settings for innovation.
alternatives.concept: Study how scientific discoveries become useful innovations. Combine entrepreneurship, economics and digital strategy with research methods, then use climate, resource use and biomedicine to explore different settings for innovation.
progression: Programming, mathematics and research foundations precede later data analysis and econometrics. Life science and business foundations precede advanced work in medicines, disease and strategy.

alternatives.label: Renewable Energy and Sustainability Innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Study renewable generation, storage and energy use, then apply technical and economic analysis to renewable system design. Examine how material reuse, environmental monitoring and governance shape energy transitions. Utrecht adds dedicated thermodynamics and transport innovation.
alternatives.concept: Study renewable generation, storage and energy use, then apply technical and economic analysis to renewable system design. Examine how material reuse, environmental monitoring and governance shape energy transitions. Utrecht adds dedicated thermodynamics and transport innovation.
progression: The sustainability gateways precede energy and environmental study. Energy & Sustainability precedes Renewable System Design, while introductory data study precedes econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: Study renewable generation, storage and energy use, then apply technical and economic analysis to renewable system design. Examine how material reuse, environmental monitoring and governance shape energy transitions. Utrecht adds dedicated thermodynamics and transport innovation. Each plan has 6 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.

alternatives.label: Life Sciences and Health Innovation
alternatives.labelReason: Study cells, human physiology, disease and medicines alongside entrepreneurship, market research and digital strategy. Use laboratory work and health psychology to explore how biomedical discoveries and health technologies can address practical needs.
alternatives.concept: Study cells, human physiology, disease and medicines alongside entrepreneurship, market research and digital strategy. Use laboratory work and health psychology to explore how biomedical discoveries and health technologies can address practical needs.
progression: Life science foundations precede cell biology, physiology and pharmacology. Cell biology precedes laboratory work and molecular pathology. Research methods and introductory data study precede econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: Study cells, human physiology, disease and medicines alongside entrepreneurship, market research and digital strategy. Use laboratory work and health psychology to explore how biomedical discoveries and health technologies can address practical needs. Each plan has 6 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.

selection.assessment: Three plans share entrepreneurship, economics, research and digital strategy. The broad plan balances environmental and biomedical applications. The energy plan adds renewable technology, system design and material recovery. The life sciences plan adds cell biology, physiology, practical laboratory work and health behavior. The specialised plans address the two official domains within UCR’s course coverage. Dedicated transport engineering, applied thermodynamics and specialist innovation projects remain material differences.

blocks: Both introduce how ventures develop and implement ideas. Utrecht focuses specifically on innovation theory.
Both study organizational strategy and technology adoption. UCR focuses on digital transformation.
Both develop quantitative analysis. UCR applies regression methods to economic questions.
Both examine organizations, teams and change. UCR emphasizes organizational psychology.
Utrecht requires a project that applies innovation methods. UCR develops related inquiry skills across courses.
Both examine economic decisions and markets. Utrecht applies these ideas to technological change.
Both use mathematics to model change, including differential equations.
Both develop research design, measurement and evidence analysis.
Utrecht studies long-term change across natural and human history in one course.
Utrecht requires a dedicated course in thermodynamics and energy conversion.
Utrecht studies innovation systems across firms, sectors and institutions. UCR addresses related governance and strategy in separate courses.
Both study energy technologies. UCR emphasizes renewable generation, storage and grid integration.
Utrecht requires an innovation project for an external client. UCR’s energy plan includes a renewable-design project for a partner.
Both consider how to deploy energy technology. UCR focuses on renewable system design, while Utrecht includes transport innovation.
Both examine energy and material use. UCR emphasizes product life cycles and reuse.
Technology ethics, thesis and profiling space
Utrecht teaches dedicated methods for assessing technologies. UCR develops related evaluation and ethical reasoning across courses.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC thesis in the chosen domain. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose 45 EC of electives, including at least 7.5 EC at advanced level in this example.

notes.text: Utrecht combines innovation studies with one science domain. The UCR options combine business, research and science, with a broad plan and two plans that emphasize energy or health.

The Utrecht example uses Energy & Transport. It includes dedicated thermodynamics, transport innovation, two innovation projects and a required thesis. Utrecht also offers a Life Sciences domain. UCR’s health plan draws on related biomedical science and laboratory work.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s mainly Dutch-taught bachelor combines natural science with the study of how technologies develop and how organizations and society adopt them.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example follows Energy & Transport and Innovation in Firms and Markets. Utrecht also offers Life Sciences and two other innovation learning lines. The three UCR options cover broad science and innovation, renewable energy, or health.
